title: Peter Thiel on Tim Ferriss: Capitalism vs. competition, no trends, and the case against lottery-ticket investing
summary: In a Q&A-style interview promoting Zero to One, Thiel argues technology matters more than globalization, that capitalism and competition are opposites, and that missions beat trends. He criticizes failure-worship, spray-and-pray investing and the education bubble, and urges starting sooner and thinking for yourself.

principles.text: Capitalism and competition are opposites: competition competes profits away, monopolies accumulate capital.
principles.quote: whereas most people believe that capitalism and competition are synonyms, I think they’re antonyms.

principles.text: Avoid trends; pursue a unique mission that no one else is solving.
principles.quote: You, generally, never want to be part of a popular trend.

principles.text: Failure is overrated: it is over-determined, teaches little, and is a tragedy, not an educational imperative.
principles.quote: I think failure is massively overrated.

principles.text: Don't treat startups as lottery tickets; concentrate and build high conviction before writing any check.
principles.quote: I think the anti lottery ticket approach is to try to be concentrated

principles.text: Never let convention substitute for truth; everyone listening to everyone about the future is the definition of a bubble.
principles.quote: we never want to let a convention be a short cut for truth.

principles.text: Stagnation is the risk, but low-hanging fruit remains and many secrets are left to unlock; innovate or face a bleak century.
principles.quote: There are many great secrets left to be unlocked in the decades ahead.
